title: Chromatic and Spherical Aberration
notes: **Chromatic aberration:** a lens fails to focus all colours at the same point because $n$ varies with wavelength. Violet focuses closer to the lens than red, producing coloured fringes around images.
**Spherical aberration:** rays passing through the edge of a spherical lens focus at a different point from rays passing through the centre. Edge rays focus closer to the lens.
**Why spherical aberration occurs:** the lens surface is part of a sphere, but the ideal focusing surface for parallel rays is a paraboloid, not a sphere.
**Reducing spherical aberration:** use a diaphragm to block marginal rays, or use a compound lens with surfaces chosen to cancel the effect.
**Relation:** chromatic aberration is a colour-dependent focal shift; spherical aberration is an aperture-dependent focal shift. Both degrade image quality in simple lenses.
